title: Lemon-Herb Cod with Roasted Vegetables
seoTitle: Lemon-Herb Cod with Roasted Vegetables | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Flaky baked cod with roasted zucchini, tomatoes, and potatoes in a lemon-herb butter
subtitle: Flaky baked cod with roasted zucchini, tomatoes, and potatoes in a lemon-herb butter
description: Cod fillets bake under a lemon-herb butter alongside zucchini, cherry tomatoes, and baby potatoes. It is a genuinely lighter dinner option with lean protein and roasted vegetables, built to be simple rather than fussy.

steps.title: Par-cook the potatoes
steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 400°F. Toss halved baby potatoes with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan and roast 15 minutes to give them a head start over the faster-cooking vegetables. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Mix the lemon-herb butter
steps.instruction: Whisk melted butter with lemon juice, garlic, parsley, and thyme in a small bowl until combined.

steps.title: Add zucchini and tomatoes
steps.instruction: Add zucchini and cherry tomatoes to the pan with the potatoes, tossing lightly with a bit more oil, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Add the cod and butter sauce
steps.instruction: Pat cod dry and season with salt and pepper. Nestle cod portions among the vegetables and spoon the lemon-herb butter evenly over the fish.

steps.title: Bake until cod flakes easily
steps.instruction: Bake 12–15 minutes until cod is opaque and flakes easily with a fork and vegetables are tender. Cod is done by texture, not just a clock — check the thickest fillet. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Hold and serve
steps.instruction: If service is delayed, hold covered loosely at 200°F for no more than 15 minutes — cod continues to firm up and can dry out if held too long. Target oven/smoker temperature: 200°F.

proTips: Prep tip: Pat cod completely dry before seasoning so the butter sauce actually clings instead of sliding off.
Rookie tip: Check cod a few minutes early — it goes from tender to dry quickly once it passes done.
Use haddock or tilapia if cod isn't available; cook times are similar.
Squeeze fresh lemon over the finished dish right before serving for extra brightness.
tonightSpread: Main: Lemon-herb cod with roasted vegetables
Sides: Crusty bread, simple green salad
Condiments: Extra lemon wedges, melted butter
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool cod and vegetables in a shallow pan within two hours; reheat gently at 300°F, not high heat.
Store cod and vegetables together — they hold reasonably well for up to 3 days.
Flake leftover cod over greens for a fast, no-cook next-day lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It gives crews a real lighter-calorie option on nights when the hall wants to ease off heavier meals, without turning dinner into a salad — everything still comes out of the oven hot and finished.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: potatoes can be par-cooked a day ahead. Storage: keep cod and vegetables together up to 3 days. Reheating: reheat covered at 300°F just until warm — cod dries out fast at high heat.
substitutions: Use haddock, tilapia, or halibut instead of cod.
Use olive oil instead of butter for a dairy-free version.
Add asparagus in place of zucchini when in season.
